# Kyoto 6-Day Trip Plan for 2 Adults

A balanced Kyoto itinerary for **2026-04-10 to 2026-04-15** with relaxed mornings, one afternoon rest block daily, temple-and-garden focus, local food, and **under 12 km walking per day**. Budget is planned for **USD 2,400 total excluding international flights**.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary

### Day 1: Arrival, Higashiyama Soft Landing
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- **Morning:** Arrive, check in, easy lunch, then a gentle start at **Kiyomizu-dera** and nearby lanes if energy is good.
- **Afternoon rest block:** Return to the hotel for a break, tea, or a short nap.
- **Evening:** Walk **Sannenzaka/Ninenzaka** at an easy pace and end with dinner in Gion.
- **Food 1:** Yudofu tofu set near Higashiyama.
- **Food 2:** Kyoto-style obanzai dinner in Gion.
- **Transit notes:** Use a taxi or bus from station to hotel; keep the first day light to stay under walking limits.

### Day 2: Arashiyama Gardens and Riverside
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Morning:** Visit **Tenryu-ji** garden, then the **Bamboo Grove** early enough to avoid the busiest crowds.
- **Afternoon rest block:** Cafe break or hotel rest after lunch.
- **Evening:** Riverside stroll near Togetsukyo Bridge, then a casual dinner.
- **Food 1:** Tofu and yuba lunch in Arashiyama.
- **Food 2:** Matcha dessert or soft-serve after the garden visit.
- **Transit notes:** JR or Hankyu to Arashiyama area; use local buses only if needed to reduce walking.

### Day 3: Northern Temples and Garden Calm
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Morning:** Start with **Kinkaku-ji**, then continue to **Ryoan-ji** for the rock garden.
- **Afternoon rest block:** Return to central Kyoto for a long break.
- **Evening:** Light dinner near your hotel or downtown.
- **Food 1:** Kyoto ramen or tsukemen for lunch.
- **Food 2:** Seasonal kaiseki-style dinner if you want a splurge night.
- **Transit notes:** This is a bus-heavy day; use taxi for one leg if you want to keep walking minimal.

### Day 4: Fushimi Inari and Sake District
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/moon-stars.svg
- **Morning:** Go to **Fushimi Inari Taisha** for a shorter torii-gate walk, stopping before the full summit to control distance.
- **Afternoon rest block:** Rest back at the hotel, then head out again later.
- **Evening:** Explore **Fushimi sake district** for a relaxed dinner and tasting.
- **Food 1:** Inari sushi or grilled skewers near the shrine.
- **Food 2:** Sake-pairing dinner or izakaya-style meal in Fushimi.
- **Transit notes:** JR Nara Line is the easiest way in; keep the shrine route partial to stay comfortably under 12 km.

### Day 5: Half-Day Shopping and Downtown Kyoto
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- **Morning:** Half-day shopping at **Nishiki Market** and nearby Teramachi/Shinkyogoku arcades.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Morning:** Half-day shopping at **Nishiki Market** and nearby Teramachi/Shinkyogoku arcades, Kyoto, Japan
- **Afternoon rest block:** Return to the hotel after lunch and shopping.
- **Evening:** Optional light stroll along the Kamo River or a calm dinner in central Kyoto.
- **Food 1:** Market snacks at Nishiki, such as tamagoyaki or pickles.
- **Food 2:** Sushi, soba, or casual tempura dinner downtown.
- **Transit notes:** This is one of the easiest days for walking; use subway or taxi for the market area if needed.

### Day 6: Garden Finish and Departure Buffer
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar.svg
- **Morning:** Visit **Kyoto Gyoen** or **Shosei-en Garden** for a final peaceful garden stop.
- **Afternoon rest block:** Pack, rest, and keep the schedule flexible for departure timing.
- **Evening:** Early dinner before leaving or heading to the airport/station.
- **Food 1:** Light soba or udon lunch.
- **Food 2:** Final Kyoto dessert or tea set before departure.
- **Transit notes:** Choose the closest garden to your hotel and leave extra time for airport/train transfers.

## Budget Plan for USD 2,400 Total

| Category | Planned Amount | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Hotel | **USD 1,050** | Mid-range 5 nights for 2 adults |
| Food & drinks | **USD 620** | Mix of casual meals, snacks, 1 nicer dinner |
| Local transit | **USD 180** | Subway, buses, occasional taxi |
| Admissions | **USD 120** | Temples, gardens, small entry fees |
| Shopping | **USD 250** | Souvenirs, tea, crafts, small gifts |
| Buffer | **USD 180** | Weather, extra taxi, incidental costs |
| Total | **USD 2,400** | Fits your cap |

## Pace and Transit Fit

- **Walking target:** Most days stay around **5–10 km**, with Day 5 likely the lightest.
- **Rest blocks:** Built into every afternoon so the trip stays comfortable.
- **Transit strategy:** Use a mix of **subway, JR, bus, and taxi** to protect energy and keep walking under your limit.
- **Best rhythm:** One major sight in the morning, one slower activity or food stop later, then downtime.
